# Your money is blocked. You deserve answers.

*By Inês, Product Designer at Pinha*  
*Tuesday, 10 November 2026*

Since Friday, you have not been able to withdraw your money from Pinha. Our payments partner, Northvale Payments, blocked all outgoing transfers on 6 November at 09:00. Deposits and round-ups have also stopped.

**Your money has not been lost. It remains in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own money. Northvale cannot use it for its own purposes. But we cannot move it until Northvale releases it.**

That distinction matters. It also does nothing to pay your rent today.

We are working to get your money moving again. We have signed a new partner, Ostra Bank in Lisbon, and filed complaints with Banco de Portugal and the Lithuanian central bank. We do not yet have a confirmed date when you will be able to withdraw.

If you need your money urgently for rent, medical costs or because you have lost your job, **email urgent@pinha.example with the subject line URGENTE.** We are trying to secure individual releases for urgent cases. We cannot guarantee those requests will succeed, but please tell us if this is your situation.

I want to explain what happened, what we got wrong and what happens next.

## What Northvale did

Northvale Payments is an e-money institution based in Vilnius. It holds the customer money behind Pinha.

On Wednesday, 4 November, Northvale sent us an email giving 30 days’ notice of “commercial termination”. The explanation was a “risk appetite review”. We have not been given a meaningful explanation beyond that.

Two days later, on Friday, 6 November, at 09:00, Northvale blocked all outgoing transfers without warning, rather than allowing the notice period it had given us.

So we received a notice saying 30 days, then lost the ability to move your money two days later.

We are angry about that. Giving notice and then blocking access before that notice runs out leaves people facing consequences they had no chance to prepare for.

But Northvale’s decision does not remove our responsibility. You chose Pinha. You should not have to understand our payments arrangements to know whether you can get your savings back.

## What “safeguarded” means—and what it does not

Your money is held in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own funds. It is not money Northvale can use to run its business.

That is why we can say your money has not been lost and remains safeguarded.

It is **not** the same as saying you can access it right now. You cannot, and neither can we. We need Northvale to release it.

I do not want to hide that behind reassuring language. Money can be protected and still be out of reach when you need it. That is the situation today, and it is serious.

## We made a mistake too

We relied on one payments partner. We did not have a backup ready.

That was our mistake. We were naive about what relying on a single partner could mean for the people using Pinha. You are now living with the consequences of that decision.

I designed the screen that says: “Your money is always yours, take it out anytime.”

I keep thinking about those words. I wrote and designed them as a promise you could rely on, not as something that would turn out to depend on a partner continuing to cooperate. Looking at that screen now makes me feel sick.

That is not something I am telling you so you will feel sorry for us. It is something we need to own. We put those words in front of you. Right now, the app cannot do what they say.

You have every reason to be angry with Northvale. You have every reason to be angry with us too. I am not going to ask you to calm down.

## What we are doing to restore access

We have already signed a new payments partner: **Ostra Bank, based in Lisbon.**

Signing the agreement is an important step, but it does not complete the move. The migration still needs:

- **Northvale to send the balances file** needed to transfer customer balances.
- **Approval from Banco de Portugal.**

Until those dependencies are resolved, we cannot give you a reliable withdrawal date.

Our current estimate for the migration is **10 to 15 working days**. That is an estimate, not a promise or a confirmed countdown. We do not have enough certainty to turn it into a calendar date, and we will not give you one just because it would make this post easier to write.

On Saturday, 7 November, we filed complaints with both Banco de Portugal and the Lithuanian central bank.

Rui, our CEO, is spending today in calls with lawyers and Banco de Portugal. The work is to get the balances released and complete the move to Ostra—not simply to get another explanation from Northvale.

## If you need your money urgently

Some of you cannot wait for a migration.

If the block is affecting your ability to pay rent or medical costs, or you have lost your job and need access to your savings, please:

1. **Email urgent@pinha.example.**
2. **Use URGENTE as the subject line.**
3. **Explain the situation and any deadline you are facing.**

We are trying to get Northvale to make individual releases for urgent cases. These releases are not guaranteed. We do not control Northvale’s decision, and we cannot promise a payment date through this route.

But we need to know which situations are urgent so we can raise them.

One message from a user in Porto has stayed with me. She had spent three years saving for a car deposit. The dealership had given her until Friday, 13 November. Her message was in capital letters.

I read it on the metro and nearly cried. There was nothing unreasonable about her anger. She had saved the money. She needed to use it. She could not.

I cannot tell her—or you—that this will be fixed by Friday. I wish I could. Giving her a date we cannot stand behind would be another way of letting her down.

## Support is taking longer than it should

Since Friday, 6 November, we have received around **1,900 support emails**. There are three people answering them, and replies are currently taking around **two days**.

That is too long when you are worried about your savings. I am telling you the numbers so you know what to expect, not because the size of our team should be your problem.

For urgent situations, please use the urgent email address and subject line above so we can identify them.

**We have also cancelled the monthly fee for November and December for everyone.** You do not need to request this.

Cancelling fees does not make up for losing access to your money. We should not be charging you while this is happening.

## When you will hear from us

We will publish updates on this blog **every Monday and Thursday until this is resolved**. The next scheduled update is Thursday, 12 November.

Those updates will say what has changed, what is still blocked and whether our estimate has changed. If we are still waiting on something, we will say that rather than dress it up as progress.

You should not have to send a support email just to find out whether anything has moved.

For now, the most important things are these: your money remains safeguarded, withdrawals are still blocked, and we do not yet have a confirmed date for restoring access. If you are facing an urgent situation, write to **urgent@pinha.example**, with **URGENTE** in the subject line.

You trusted us with money you were putting aside for something. We failed to make sure you could keep accessing it when our relationship with a partner went wrong. We owe you an apology for that—and, more importantly, the work of getting it back within your reach.

**Inês**
